text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the schema RFC — we just started seeing a handful of traces where trace.meta.user_id became trace.context.end_user.id after the tracing lib bump. This breaks a bunch of late-enrich logic and billing-key propagation. Can we sync on a pragmatic bridge strategy?

dan: Ugh. Is this limited to the new SDK version or did the proxy also rewrite keys?

maria: Looks like SDK+agent. Examples:
```
# old
trace.meta.user_id: "u123"
# new
trace.context.end_user.id: "u123"
```

kevin: Thanks for the sample. Two obvious options: 1) adaptor at the edge/proxy that normalizes to the old envelope field (fast to roll, minimal downstream change), or 2) push consumers to accept both keys (changes across many services).

olivia: Edge adaptor sounds fine but watch perf and ops complexity. We already have hot paths in the ingress proxy. Adding normalization could increase CPU on the busiest routes.

samir: Another hybrid: add a light-weight adapter in the gateway that normalizes only for tenants who opt-in to legacy compatibility. Default behavior is pass-through for new SDK users. That reduces blast radius and lets us turn off adapter when clients upgrade.

kevin: Agree hybrid is safest. Implementation idea: add a small wasm filter that maps `trace.context.end_user.id -> trace.meta.user_id` and vice-versa for downstream queries. Wasm keeps overhead bounded and is easy to toggle per-tenant.

maria: Good. Two more constraints: 1) any adapter must preserve sampling + billing keys so cost attribution doesn't regress, 2) we need a short-lived fallback in the enrichment pipeline so late-joined traces don't get lost.

olivia: For (1) we should ensure adapter copies `billing.key` and `trace.sample_reason` untouched. For (2) enrichment can have a fallback step that looks at both shapes when matching. That can live in the stitcher with a feature flag.

kevin: Implementation checklist I'm hearing:
- wasm adapter in edge (per-tenant toggle)
- adapter preserves billing/sample attributes verbatim
- stitcher fallback to accept both shapes for 8 weeks
- telemetry + perf dashboard to watch adapter CPU + latency impact

maria: Perfect. Also we should add a short-lived compatibility test in our CI that injects both envelopes and verifies downstream billing keys don't drop.

dan: Who owns the wasm adapter work? I can take the prototype if you want, kevin can review.

kevin: Happy to review and help with perf knobs. I'll put a wasm runtime perf checklist together (cpu perf, allocs, cold-starts).

samir: I'll add the stitcher fallback change and the feature flag. We should coordinate rollout windows. Suggest adapter -> canary -> 10% -> 100% over 48 hours, then enable stitcher fallback for the same duration.

maria: Sounds like a plan. Action items: dan proto wasm adapter, kevin perf checklist + review, samir stitcher change + flag, olivia will own telemetry dashboards and thresholds. I'll open a follow-up RFC with the rollout timeline and required tests.

ingest-bot: deploy: wasm-adapter-proto -> staging succeeded (1766550200) :white_check_mark:

kevin: Nice, can we get some staging traces with both shapes to validate?

dan: Pushed a small test harness to staging that emits both envelopes every 10s. Link: https://staging-ci.internal/runs/wasm-compat-check

olivia: Dashboard query I'm using: `sum(rate(http_request_duration_ms[1m])) by (tenant, adapter_present)` — will add a panel for adapter CPU and 95th p99 latency.

maria: If we see >2% tail increase or adapter CPU >8% of proxy node, we abort and iterate. Otherwise go forward.

samir: I'll coordinate the 10% canary and set a rollback playbook.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll drop the RFC/rollout doc in #eng-platform and ping for final sign-off once the staging results look good. :thumbsup:
